item.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
item.lesson: Jan van Eyck did not invent oil painting, but he perfected it so thoroughly that legend credited him with its invention for centuries. Where Italian painters worked in fast-drying egg tempera, van Eyck built up translucent oil glazes that let light pass through layers of color and bounce back — which is why the brass chandelier gleams, the fur looks soft, and the oranges by the window still seem ripe after almost six hundred years. The couple is probably Giovanni di Nicolao Arnolfini, an Italian merchant living in Bruges, with his wife, though what exactly the scene records — a betrothal, a marriage, a memorial — is still argued. On the back wall, above the mirror, the artist wrote in flourished script: 'Johannes de eyck fuit hic. 1434' — Jan van Eyck was here.
item.lookFor: Look into the convex mirror on the back wall: it reflects the whole room in miniature, including two tiny figures standing where you, the viewer, stand.
